messages:
Laura M: quick run of L4 vs T4 vs A10G for two workloads: embeddings (batch embed 256) and small-chat (chat-7b-ish, 512 context). pasted high-level numbers below, looking for sizing recs + kernel notes. chart: https://redwood-internal/bench/1799994321/summary.png

Arjun S: nice — can you drop the commands you used? want to reproduce in eu-west1.

Laura M: yep, script:```./bench_runner --model open-small-chat-7b --workloads embeddings,chat_small --regions us-east1,eu-west1,asia-southeast1 --gpus L4,T4,A10G --batch-embed 256 --chat-batch 8 --context 512 --quant q4_0,q8_0 --runs 3```

Sam K: top-level takeaways?

Laura M: summary: A10G best throughput across both. For embeddings A10G ~2400 emb/s, L4 ~1600 emb/s, T4 ~950 emb/s (all per GPU). For small-chat (seq=512, batching 8) A10G p95 token latency 38ms, L4 p95 ~55ms, T4 p95 ~110ms. cost/unit (raw infra): A10G cost index 1.0, L4 ~0.6, T4 ~0.25 (so cost/throughput shows L4 often sweet spot for embeddings).

Hana L: interesting — did you try enabling prefix/KV cache? that changes p95 for chat a lot.

Laura M: yes — KV caching on for steady-state. numbers above are with KV cache warm. cold-start chat p95 on T4 spikes to 320ms.

Mike P: what about quantization? quality regressed?

Laura M: q4_0 on embeddings: negligible difference (cosine delta <0.002). For chat, q4_0 adds small fluency hit on longer contexts — we ran our Evals set and saw a 3.5% drop in helpfulness metric vs fp16. q8_0 maintained quality but slower than q4_0 on T4 due to kernel support.

Arjun S: kernel notes? which kernels used per GPU?

Laura M: A10G used tuned flash-attn + triton kernels, TF32 on matmul paths. L4 used newer int8-fused GEMM kernels (good for q4), sometimes falls back to slower cuBLAS paths for certain seq lengths >1024. T4 frequently hit fallback to cuBLAS on chat causing the big latency hit.

Sam K: region differences? anything surprising?

Laura M: us-east1 had best p95 for A10G (lowest network variance). eu-west1 ~+6% p95, asia-southeast1 ~+12% p95 for chat with same SKU — mostly networking and cooler bin of T4 fleet caused extra variance. embeddings less sensitive.

bench-bot: automated summary: embeddings per-gpu: A10G=2400/s, L4=1600/s, T4=950/s. chat tokens/sec per-gpu (batch8): A10G=820 tok/s, L4=520 tok/s, T4=220 tok/s. see /artifacts/1799994321/*.csv

Hana L: sounds like recommendation: use L4 for mid-size embedding fleets (better cost/throughput), use A10G for chat-critical low-latency paths. T4 only for extremely cost-constrained non-latency SLOs. agree?

Laura M: yep. additional note: for embeddings at scale, shard across L4 with batching 256 + async prefetch — we saw near-linear scale to 8 GPUs. for chat, prefer A10G with q8_0+kv-cache and canual kernel pinning to avoid cuBLAS fallback.

Mike P: any docs for kernel pinning?

Laura M: added quick howto:```# tune config
export REDWOOD_INFER_KERNEL=PILOT_TRITON
export REDWOOD_QUANT_MODE=q8_0
./serve --model open-small-chat-7b --max-seq 512 --kv-cache on --batch-size 8
```

Arjun S: will spin this up in eu-west1 A10G pool tomorrow, thanks.

Sam K: can you attach the per-run csvs? want to feed into cost calc.

Laura M: uploaded: https://redwood-internal/bench/1799994321/artifacts.zip (csvs + charts + eval diffs). will follow up with sizing table tomorrow. :thumbsup:
